{{Quote|Long ago the Rakata ruled all the known galaxy; all species bowed down to us.|Keeper [[Orsaa]]|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
The '''Rakata''', also known as the '''Builders''', were an ancient [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with distinctive amphibian features [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]]. They were technologically advanced and one of the earliest [[Spacefaring/Legends|spacefaring]] races that once [[Infinite Empire/Legends|ruled]] [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in its [[Pre-Republic era|distant past]] and created early [[Force-drive|hyperdrive technology]]. The long-term use of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] corrupted their society and turned them into a race of merciless warriors. The Rakata used their potent technologies to conquer and [[Slavery/Legends|enslave]] every other species they came across throughout the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. During their reign, they were characterized by their cruelty, savagery, and arrogance. They were known to strip entire planets of their resources, [[Terraforming/Legends|terraform]] worlds to fit their own shifting needs and kill entire slave workforces; and to eat and defile the bodies of slain enemies and even members of their own species.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|In all of our travels, never had we encountered a species that lived only to conquer and destroy. The Rakata cannibalized their own.|Master [[A'nang]]|<ref name="DOTJ 9">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Rakata_profile.png|thumb|left|150px|A Rakata]]
In appearance, Rakata were smooth skinned<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> amphibian-like<ref name="SW:DJ0">[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0|''Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi'' 0]]</ref> humanoids that had tall craniums along with eyes that protruded from each side of their heads on short stalks. These bipedal beings had three digit hands that were tipped with claws for digging through packed dirt. As a species, they were uniformly lean and close to the same height. Outsiders had some difficulty in distinguishing between individual Rakata although females tended to have a more slender build.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> The dentition of Rakata, consisting of a multitude of sharp teeth, reflected the carnivorous habits of the members of this species, even known for eating members of sentient species, including other Rakata.

Skin tones amongst their kind tended to be gray or gray-brown.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> Almost all Rakata had gray or reddish-gray skin, though this was a trait of the dominant lineage of those that survived the ancient plague that thinned their numbers. Among the more rare specimens were the near extinct breeds which included the blue skinned [[Droot]], red striped [[Ikalik]], and black [[Bukesek]].<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> The Rakata were originally a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Species/Legends|species]], though they became blind to the Force as a result of a plague that afflicted their race.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

==History==
===Rise of the Rakata===
{{Quote|The Rakata are a pestilence upon the Galaxy that, to our shame, we, the Kwa, unleashed.|Master [[A'nang]]|<ref name="DOTJ 9" />}}
[[File:Rakata_First_Contact.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The First Contact between the then-primitive Rakata, and the benevolent Kwa]]
The Rakata species originated on the planet [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]], a temperate terrestrial world in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].<ref name="KOTORCG" /><ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before [[36,453 BBY]], the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]]—a Force-sensitive reptilian species from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]—arrived on Lehon, the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Rakata species, via their [[Infinity Gate]] technology that allowed the Kwa to travel instantaneously across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. As they had done on many worlds before, the Kwa became the Rakata's benefactors, teaching them about [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and giving them advanced technology.<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> Around this time, the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] themselves (the backers of the Kwa and then the dominant galactic power) also made the Rakata one of their slave races.<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> However, the Kwa were horrified to realize that Rakata were a [[Cannibalism|cannibalistic]] race that ignored the Kwa teachings of balance, drawing only on the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Pairing their aggression and desire for conquest with the Kwa technology, the Rakata expanded out from Lehon and began to conquer other worlds in the Unknown Regions.<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> The establishment of their [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] was centered on their homeworld of Lehon, and they used [[Force-drive|Force-based hyperdrives]] to travel to worlds with strong Force signatures.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

The Infinite Empire, as the Rakata called themselves, targeted worlds that were rich with the Force, which they conquered and then enslaved their populations. The Rakata developed technology that allowed them to induce fear and hatred in Force-sensitive beings, and they used the Force-sensitive [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] among the populations they conquered to fuel their warships and technology by placing them in machines that converted the slaves' dark-side emotions into energy. Desiring the Kwa's Infinity Gate technology, they turned on their benefactors when the Kwa refused—and in the [[Battle between the Kwa and the Rakata|resultant battle]] on Lehon, many Kwa [[Death/Legends|died]] holding off the Rakatan warriors so that they could destroy the gate on Lehon.<ref name="DOTJ 9" />

Though the exact circumstances of the Infinite Empire's rise to dominance were lost by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic]] specialists like [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Insmot Bowen]] generally accepted that the Rakata [[Rakatan revolt|revolted]] against the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] and fought to exterminate them.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> Building an enormous [[Space station/Legends|space station]] known as the [[Star Forge]] over the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Abo]] in the [[Lehon system]]—a factory powered by the dark side that produced warships and technology for the empire—the Rakata spread out over the Unknown Regions and into the eastern galaxy by [[35,000 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR" />

Some hypotheses over the [[Western barrier|hyperspace turbulence]] west of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] that later stopped [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] exploration of the Unknown Regions claimed that it was created by the Celestials in an effort to hold back the upstart Rakata. Despite the best efforts of the Celestials, in time, their influence declined at the hands of the Rakata. The ancient grimoires of the [[Gree Enclave/Legends|Gree Enclave]] recorded that the Rakata, whom they identified as the "Soul Hunters," unleashed curses on the work of Celestials, which they called the "Gray Swallowing" and the "Faceless Mouths," and further referred to them as the "Hollowers of Beings" and the "Eaters of Worlds."<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="Author's Cut" /> By [[33,598 BBY]], the Infinite Empire had taken center stage<ref name="KotOR Kashyyyk date">In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] interface of the [[Builder Forge]] asserts that the computer was last accessed by the [[Rakata/Legends|Builders]] 29,642 standard years before [[3956 BBY]].</ref> and by [[30,000 BBY]] the Celestials had vanished from the galaxy.<ref name="TEA" />

===The Infinite Empire===
{{Quote|I am Rakata—it is the name of my people. Eons ago, our Infinite Empire ruled this world and so many others.|The Imprisoned One|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:ConstructionOfTheStarForge.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Slaves construct the [[Star Forge]].]]
At its zenith, the Infinite Empire linked over five hundred<ref name="History 5">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 05: Rise of the Infinite Empire}}</ref> Force-rich worlds all across the galaxy. Their extensive civilization was spread across countless star systems and was much larger than later-era empires.<ref name="TJoMGD">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']]</ref> Through the use of dark-side-fueled technologies such as Force-powered hyperdrive, the Builders' Infinite Empire dominated known space for thousands of years. Many of the most prominent worlds of the galaxy were included in this empire, such as [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Honoghr/Legends|Honoghr]], [[Generis/Legends|Generis]], [[Hijarna]], [[Xo]], and [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]. However, their hyperdrives could only visit worlds possessing strong Force signatures, resulting in huge voids between their conquered worlds. The haphazard nature of their empire allowed numerous other civilizations to flourish, and loose confederacies of other civilizations developed in the spaces between Rakatan worlds through the use of dangerous as well as unpredictable hyperdrive technology.<ref name="TEA" />

Being a warlike and cruel race, the great danger posed by the Rakata was the fact that they were strong in the Force along with being technologically advanced. They were known to enslave or wipe out every civilization they encountered.<ref name="Codex: Rakata">{{TORcite|type=codex|Rakata}}</ref> They were also known to have had been both cruel and manipulative masters of those they enslaved.<ref name="TEA" /> At its height, the Empire's population numbered ten billion Rakatan warriors and over a trillion slaves. Among its conquests were the [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]] of [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]],<ref name="KOTOR" /> [[Kumumgah/Legends|Kumumgah]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]] of Honoghr,<ref name="TEA" /> [[Human/Legends|Humans]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], and the natives of the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> By transporting these slave species to new worlds, the Rakata were believed to have inadvertently seeded swaths of the galaxy with sentient life.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Furthermore, they made use of [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] workers and [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] slaves to create weapons of colossal scale.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> On [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]] millennia ago, beautiful crystal formations were shaped by slaves of the Infinite Empire to commemorate a long-forgotten victory.<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', Archaeology mission "Caught in Crystal"</ref> At its peak, nearly five hundred conquered worlds paid tribute to the Rakata Infinite Empire.<ref name="Codex: Rakata" />

The forest world of Kashyyyk was one world captured by the Empire, and the Rakata installed a [[Builder Forge|terraforming computer]] on the planet to manipulate Kashyyyk's [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|wroshyr trees]]. However, the computer lost contact with the Rakata in [[33,598 BBY]], and [[33,357 BBY|over two hundred years later]] it malfunctioned, causing a hyper-acceleration in the growth of the wroshyrs.<ref name="KOTOR" /> During the [[Annexation of Kwa holdings|annexation]] of the [[Kwa holdings]], the Rakata brutally subjugated Dathomir, the homeworld of the Kwa,<ref name="TEA" /> in revenge for the Kwa's destruction of their Infinity Gates across the galaxy,<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> and as a result the Kwa eventually devolved into the simpleminded [[Kwi]] lizards.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> According to the beliefs of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], the usage of the Kwa Infinity Gates created unnatural voids and wounds to Dathomir that saw the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]] call the Infinite Empire to the planet. Their arrival decimated the Kwa who were transformed into an animal state by the action of the Spirits.<ref name="BoS:SftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Intrigued by the enormous [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]] native to Dathomir, the Infinite Empire transported a number of them back to Lehon as curiosities, and they also succeeded in [[Defeat of the Gree Empire|driving]] the [[Gree/Legends|Gree]]—another spacefaring species at the [[Time/Legends|time]]—all the way back to their [[Gree Enclave/Legends|home cluster]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Infinite Empire introduced a rancor to the planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], where it became a mythological creature in the culture of the native [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]].<ref name="Barely">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-2|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> The Infinite Empire turned the planet [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] into a prison world, using stasis technology to entomb monsters, warlords, and other powerful entities.<ref name="History of Belsavis Prison">{{TORcite|type=codex|History of Belsavis Prison}}</ref> The first prisoner of Belsavis—and the reason the prison was constructed—was the [[World Razer]], a mysterious being whose hunger supposedly consumed a thousand worlds. According to inscriptions in [[the Tomb]], which was the Galactic Republic's term for the primary Rakatan prison complex, it took the entire Infinite Empire to subdue the World Razer.<ref name="World Razer">{{TORcite|type=codex|The World Razer}}</ref>

At some unknown point, the Infinite Empire came under threat from a marauding horde of aliens known as the [[Esh-kha]]. These aliens raided world after world where they destroyed their inhabitants before continuing their campaign. Such actions led to the loss of several Rakatan slave worlds to the Esh-kha before the Infinite Empire assembled its military might to challenge this threat. The Rakata hated the Esh-kha and referred to them as a plague on the galaxy due to their actions. The resultant conflict engulfed the entire galaxy and led to the near extinction of the Esh-kha. Only a hundred thousand survivors lived by the time the Infinite Empire won the war with these remaining Esh-kha being imprisoned on Belsavis where they were placed in stasis. The technology preserved the species but left them conscious with the Rakata believing that such a punishment would teach the Esh-kha the error of their ways. The reputation of the Esh-kha led to the Infinite Empire even imprisoning [[Hallow Voice]] and his peaceful Esh-kha followers on Belsavis. The great victory achieved by the Infinite Empire led to the Rakata creating a monument on the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] that contained an interactive hologram that spoke of their victory over the Esh-kha.<ref name="TOR" />

During their period of expansion, the Rakata encountered the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. At first, the Rakata pretended to ally themselves with the warlord [[Adas]], going so far as to show him how to construct the pyramidal [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocron]]. In time, Adas learned that the invaders were bent on [[Invasion of Korriban|conquest]].<ref name="END:TSD">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Unifying the Sith, King Adas led a revolt against the Rakata invaders and subsequently acquired their technology as well as that of [[Holocron/Legends|Holocrons]].<ref name="JvS:TEGF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> When the two species went to war, he managed to lead the Sith to victory and drive the Rakata from Korriban, but at the expense of his life.<ref name="END:TSD" /> Though defeated, the Rakata had devastated Korriban, which led to the Sith's relocation to [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]].<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> The actions of the Infinite Empire led to the Sith truly embracing the dark side, and their conflict prompted a [[Kissai heretics|group of Sith priests]] to form a [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|splinter cult]] that became convinced by their interactions with the Rakata that all sentient species were Force-sensitive.<ref name="Karnak Tetsu Web Enhancement">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben5|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 5: Karnak Tetsu, Sorcerer of Tund}}</ref> At some point, a Rakata called [[Soa]] formed his own empire that was based at Korriban that served as his throne. However, the Infinite Empire later imprisoned him in the [[Eternity Vault]] on Belsavis, where he became known as the Infernal One.<ref name="TOR" />

The height of the Rakata was reached around [[25,793 BBY]], when their Infinite Empire had reached its zenith.<ref name="SW:DJ0" /> By that time, they had meddled in the ecosystems of many of the worlds under their reign ranging from Kashyyyk to Tatooine<ref name="TEA" /> and [[Vagar Praxut]].<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> The surface of Kashyyyk was specifically terraformed by the Rakata for agricultural purposes.<ref name="KOTOR" /> In contrast, worlds such as [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] and [[Morseer]] were stripped bare during the height of the Infinite Empire.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> At some point, they took control over the planet [[Byss/Legends|Byss]], which became their stronghold for exploring the forbidden reaches of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> It was here that they discovered a powerful world deep in the Core that was thought impossible to reach.

===Encountering the Je'daii===
{{Quote|My Hound, Trill, claims she has sensed a Force-rich world within the Deep Core.|Predor [[Skal'nas]]|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
At the Infinite Empire's peak, the Rakata used slaves trained as [[Force Hound]]s. They were beings trained in the dark side meant to locate planets strong in the Force. Such was the case of Tython, located by [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]], the servant of [[Predor]] Tul'kar. In this time the Force Hound Trill claimed to have detected a world incredibly strong in the Force, but that it was impossible to reach from the twisting lanes caused by the black holes and stars. Xesh was sent to reach this planet by Predor [[Skal'nas]]. Tython was an isolated planet with a population of trained Force-sensitives calling themselves Je'daii. The Je'daii strove to balance their actions between dark and light, lest they ignite massive Force Storms across the entire planet. Xesh made it to Tython, but his dark presence shifted the balance of the planet, causing an intense planet-wide storm. This storm both alerted the Je'daii and damaged the ship, resulting in its crash and destruction on Tython. The servant of the Rakata was the lone survivor and immediately was confronted by Je'daii.

===Collapse===
{{Quote|During the collapse of the Rakata Empire, the warlords unleashed weapons of terrible destruction that threatened to drive our species to extinction.|Rakatan Elder to Revan|translated=1|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
After generations of galactic supremacy, the Infinite Empire began to fracture and around [[25,200 BBY]] the Rakatan empire imploded.<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> Constant tensions between internal factions suddenly erupted into a devastating [[Rakatan Civil War|civil war]] caused by the Star Forge's corrupting influence. Already weakened by warfare, the Rakata were suddenly struck by a deadly plague that spread rapidly through their ranks<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> and decimated the species.<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> It was later theorized that the disease was created by a slave species because it had only infected the Builders themselves. The virulent plague nearly exterminated the Rakata and brought the Infinite Empire to its knees, but the worst was yet to come.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> The Rakata suddenly and inexplicably began to lose their connection to the Force. Worse, they were unable to uncover the source of their failing sensitivity. Rakatan scientists came up with numerous speculative hypotheses to explain their worsening condition, but in the end, all of their guesses proved incorrect.<ref name="KOTOR" /> In time, it would be revealed that a mysterious mutation in the plague had caused it to strip the Builders of their powers.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

Thus, the rapid expansion of the Rakata came to an abrupt end when this strange plague swept through their species. Millions died as a result and those that survived had lost their connection to the Force.<ref name="Codex: Rakata" /> As the Force users were culled from the overall population at an ever increasing rate, the Rakata lost their ability to manipulate their own technology. Soon, they were forced to rely on inferior devices that were not dependent on the Force. Sensing weakness, slave species rebelled in large-scale insurrections on many member worlds and stemmed the total collapse of the Infinite Empire in [[25,200 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> As a result of this vulnerability, the Rakata were unable to suppress the massive outbreak of violent slave rebellions and uprisings against their rule.<ref name="Codex: Rakata" /> The nearly decimated Rakata could do nothing but abandon their conquests and retreat to the safety of their homeworld of Lehon.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Some Rakata castoffs survived the fall of the Infinite Empire in the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] as late as [[25,100 BBY]], allowing Tion Humans access to their Force-sensitive technology.

[[File:Unkwldtemple.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Temple of the Ancients]]]]

The loss of the Force combined with facing near extinction led the Rakata to retreat to their homeworld.<ref name="Codex: Rakata Tribes">{{TORcite|type=codex|Rakata Tribes}}</ref> By this point, the Lehon system was protected by a disruptor field that could disable any incoming ship's [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|communications]] and [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigational]] systems. The field, operated from the summit of a [[Temple of the Ancients|Temple]] on the surface of Lehon, was originally constructed to protect the Star Forge, but it was now used to protect the Rakata themselves.<ref name="KOTOR" /> On their homeworld, Rakatan civilization rapidly faded into obscurity and barbarism.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> On Lehon, a few thousand Rakata survivors seemingly represented all that remained of the Infinite Empire who remained on their hidden homeworld, where they descended into barbarity.<ref name="Codex: Rakata" /> Their infighting amongst themselves brought the remains of their civilization to even further ruin. After the global war ended, all that remained were a number of barbaric tribes. These savage Rakata dominated their isolated homeworld for the next twenty thousand years. Some of the tribes lived contently alone deep within the jungles whilst others aggressively expanded and conquered the other tribes in an effort to unite the world under a single warlord. However, each time this occurred, a revolt would erupt among the subtribes, and the cycle of conquest repeated itself again and again.<ref name="Codex: Rakata Tribes" /> Warlords devastated the surface of the planet with weapons of mass destruction, and the majority of the Rakata were forced to flee underground. Years later, when the Rakata resurfaced, they called themselves the [[Black Rakata]]. Only the descendants of the Priest Caste, the [[Elders (Rakatan)|Elders]] tribe, remained on the surface protected by their ancient temples and enclaves. They were called Red Rakata by the other Rakata tribes. They alone retained full knowledge of the potent technology and turbulent history of their species.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

In the following centuries, the Builders were purposely erased from the records of their slave subjects, and the Infinite Empire slipped from the pages of galactic history.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> In time, the liberated worlds destroyed the Rakata's creations and records so that all trace and knowledge of them was wiped from the greater galaxy.<ref name="Codex: Rakata" /> A number of Rakata tribes in the Unknown Regions were known to have stolen whatever they were capable of carrying from the storehouses of the idle Star Forge before fleeing in advance of the nuclear war that emerged between the warrior and priest classes. These refugees would later settle a region of space that became known as the [[Rakatan Archipelago]].<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> A small group of Rakata remained on the prison world of Belsavis, where they created an artificial intelligence called the [[Mother Machine]] which created entire species in a desperate attempt to recreate the lost Rakatan Force-sensitivity.<ref name="TEA" /> With the collapse of the Rakata Empire, reverse engineering began on the Rakatan hyperdrives, which led to a second wave of colonization that enveloped a small patch of the Core.<ref name="TEA" /> In [[12,293 BBY]], an expedition to [[Tandun III]] led by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Beramsh]] encountered a planet that was studded with ruins of ancient population centers. Beramsh posited that these structures were built by the Rakata.<ref name="MFn">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref>

===Remnants===
{{Quote|The few surviving Rakata declined to leave their ancestral home, and their numbers were insufficient to maintain a viable gene pool. Within a few generations, the long, slow extinction of their species was finally complete.|From the official Republic threat dossier regarding the planet Lehon|<ref name="Unknown Regions" />}}
[[File:RakataTemple.png|thumb|left|250px|Rakata near the Temple of the Ancients]]
The surviving Rakata devolved into barbarism and eventually forgot how to operate their own technology.<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> More than 20,000 years after the fall of the Infinite Empire, most Rakata had only just begun to reemerge onto the surface, yet the Elders Tribe still thrived within their secluded compound. After millennia of solitude and contemplation, the Elders desired to destroy their great factory so that they could finally put their bloody past behind them, but there was a problem. They could no longer enter their own Temple of the Ancients, the nexus of their collected knowledge and the key to accessing the Star Forge, because the Force was lost to them.<ref name="KOTOR" />

Darth [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak]]'s timely arrival in the system gave the Elders a perfect opportunity. Promising to destroy the Star Forge, Revan entered the temple, but he betrayed the Elders' trust and took the space station for himself. Around [[3959 BBY]], he harnessed the full power of the Star Forge and began a massive military invasion of the Galactic Republic that would culminate in the [[Jedi Civil War]]. Meanwhile, the Rakata were forced to watch their species' actions repeat themselves through Revan, powerless to stop it. Their Temple and Star Forge became the dwellings of dark-side users once more.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Yet Revan returned, unlooked-for, three years later and redress that betrayal. A redeemed Revan ended the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] occupation of the Rakatan temple and deactivated the planet's disruptor field so that the Star Forge could be destroyed by a Republic fleet. He also aided the Rakata's efforts to regain their lost Force sensitivity, which they believed would eventually allow them to rejoin the galactic community.<ref name="KOTOR" />

Following the destruction of the Star Forge, these Rakata joined the Galactic Republic leading to some leaving their homeworld along with their brethren behind on Lehon in order to rejoin a technologically advanced society. These travelers spread stories about their ancient society though few believed or took notice of them.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> By this age, there were still surviving Rakata, but the secrets of their ancient forebears and question on the collapse of their empire remained a mystery. Some believed Revan had uncovered a great deal about the Rakata, but his knowledge became lost when he departed known space.<ref name="TJoMGD" /> Because all records of the Infinite Empire were lost to time, some were skeptical of the notion that the seemingly primitive beings had once ruled hundreds of worlds and dominated the galaxy.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> Lehon's planetary population would continue to dwindle in time.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> This led to the Rakata of Lehon slowly dying out, as there were too few to maintain their species, but the few colonies they founded on other planets after their rediscovery managed to survive.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> By [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the Rakata on Lehon had died out and become extinct,<ref name="DB:PD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> leaving the refugees in the Rakatan Archipelago as the only survivors.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

===Legacy of the Builders===
{{Quote|You think this is plausible? I thought half of that stuff was a myth. I mean, the Rakatans?|Khedryn Faal to Jaden Korr|<ref name="Rn">[[Riptide (novel)|''Riptide'']]</ref>}}
[[File:TURSluissiRakata.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Rakatan warrior being pinned down by weapon fire]]
Though seemingly extinct on Lehon, the legacy of the Rakata still had an impact on the galaxy in later years. Scientists considered the belief that the Rakatan Infinite Empire being part of fringe science at best though some noted their similarity to the machinery located within the Kashyyyk [[Shadowlands/Legends|Shadowlands]]. In the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], numerous attempts were made at uncovering Rakatan relics with an [[Imperial Reclamation Service]] effort on Tatooine discovering an archaeological mission conducted by [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]]. They in turn had recovered the prison that contained the mind of [[The Imprisoned One]], who was accidentally released. This Rakata intended to begin the age of a new Infinite Empire through the advanced technology available to him until he was defeated.<ref name="TOR" />

During the attack on Belsavis, the Eternity Vault was pierced, leading to combat with the Infernal One, Soa. Warden [[Gorshaa]] was a Rakata still alive in the deep levels of Belsavis, where he encountered a [[Sith Inquisitor]] and offered the Sith knowledge on controlling their capabilities on the condition that the Imperial submitted their genetic material to the Mother Machine. Another Rakata still alive was [[Lhunu]], who intended to repent for his people's crimes by freeing the Esh-kha Hallow Voice and his followers with the aid of the [[The Barsen'thor|Scorekeeper's Herald]]. The Rakatan machinery in the [[Ancient Prison Caverns|Deep Prisons]] was also being sabotaged by the Esh-kha, who attempted to free more of their kin which led to Rakata holographic interface requesting travelers in repairing the machinery. The Sith in the meantime attempted to recover Rakatan memory cores in order to discern the technology used to create the prison in order to duplicate the feat so that the Empire could build their own prison world.<ref name="TOR" /> Around this time, Revan sought the destruction of the Sith and marshalled the [[Order of Revan]] cult to serve him. Their actions saw them use Rakata technology to create the powerful cyborgs of the [[Infinite Army]] with the Revanites establishing a base on Rakata Prime. A number of the native savage Rakata served Revan and battled those forces seeking to stop his plans.<ref name="TOR:SOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan]]''</ref>

By the time [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] arrived on Lehon in search of [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron]], the planet was completely devoid of sentient life.<ref name="DB:PD" /> The Sith Lord [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] was known to have collected the ancient history of the Rakata and remarked to his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] that they had made the Force subservient to their will whilst never pronouncing judgment over their works.<ref name="SW:DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

Among the only survivors of this race remained within the Unknown Regions in the Rakatan Archipelago. No Republic surveyors ever located this area of space, whilst many of the local species were abused by this pocket civilization. The other powers of the Unknown Regions were largely unaware and ignorant of the threat of these Rakata, though the Rakata themselves would flee from the [[Vagaari Empire]]'s forces. The few Rakata that remained in this space consisted of a scattering of planets where these Rakata tribes continued their ancient struggles. While most tribes were primitive and were restricted to a single planet, some had rediscovered the secrets of space flight; two tribes had even begun construction on small (half-kilometer) orbital factories similar in function to the Star Forge. Other tribes had wiped themselves or each other out with weapons they no longer understood, leaving worlds wastelands. It was believed that if any of these Rakata found a way of restoring their primeval technology, then they may have brought about the rise of the Infinite Empire once more.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

Agents of the [[One Sith]] discovered Rakatan ruins in the Unknown Regions and pillaged [[Mindspear]]s from them at some point before [[41 ABY|41.5 ABY]]. Lessons about the Rakata were taught to students of the [[Jedi academy]], where it was known that their Infinite Empire collapsed as the result of some great catastrophe. In that time, [[Jaden Korr]] encountered a structure that [[Marr Idi-Shael]] believed may have been Rakatan in origin. They later confirmed its ties with the Rakata and encountered the entity known as [[Mother (Rakatan entity)|Mother]].<ref name="Rn" />

The Rakata remained as one of the most important species for professors in the fields of planetary archaeology and xenoanthropology as they held a link to a long-ago past that changed the galaxy forever.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> By later eras, there were only a few scant ruins of their civilization which were scattered around the galaxy and provided a source of interest for archaeologists and historians.<ref name="Rn" />

==Society==
{{Quote|The Rakata are by nature a cruel and savage species.|Rakata computer to Revan|translated=1|<ref name="KOTOR" />}}
[[File:Rakata-TUR.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A group of Rakata wielding various weapons]]
By nature, the Rakata were conquerors, with many agreeing that they showed outward signs of malice, and their violent cores erupted to the surface if pushed. Enraged Rakata were incapable of being reasoned with and ignored their own injuries in their desire to destroy those they believed to be their enemies.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> Their species had shown a methodical malice in their interactions with other races.<ref name="Karnak Tetsu Web Enhancement" /> Later-era Rakata, though often primitive, knew they were once much more powerful and so were driven by a great desire to restore their species to its former glory. These Rakata were seemingly at a disadvantage in galactic society due to their primitive upbringing though their intelligence allowed them to learn to use advanced technology.<ref name="KOTORCG" />

Worlds strong in the Force were sought out by Force-sensitives called [[Force Hound]]s.<ref name="SW:DJ0" /> Once located, these worlds were explored by the Rakata and as many natives as possible enslaved through the use of technological show of force. Following the planet's capitulation, the Rakata used the same equipment to strip-mine the planet of its metals, ores, compressed gasses and radioactive plasma. Their ships typically arrived on rich unspoiled biospheres, and thus the Rakata seldom had to deal with advanced civilizations.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> At the height of the Infinite Empire, political and military maneuvering was a bloody game. Predor Tul'kar had an incredibly powerful Force Hound and would kill any who dared to claim his services, including a superior like Skal'nas, and even killed and ate his spies when they were too obvious about their treachery. As such Skal'nas had spies in his ranks and was known by his own people's standards to be brutal, having risen through the ranks by sheer will and determination. Predors laid claim to the planet they conquered, both the honor of conquest and the spoils that came with it; and they were particularly defensive and aggressive about keeping their claims, willing to challenge their superiors in order to remind them who had the claim.

The species was divided into numerous classes with the ruling group being their priest class, the members of which wore long robes with electronic control devices on their forearms and were responsible for deciphering dead texts. In contrast, members of the warrior class typically wore angular plastoid armor and carried shocklances. Those born in more primitive tribes tended to wear armor made of wood and twine, often brandishing fire-blackened spears. This division between thinkers and soldiers existed even among the most backward planets under Rakata rule. Warriors tended to be darkly suspicious of the priests, whom they saw as harnessing powers beyond comprehension, whilst the priests in turn were wary of the warriors, who they believed possessed great physical strength yet lacked brains.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

[[File:Infinite_Empire_JMGD.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The ancient Rakata]]
As a result of the ancient plague that decimated the species, Rakata of later eras were all Force-blind. They longed to restore their Force-sensitivity and felt this loss on a spiritual level, describing it as a black hole in their chests that consumed their life, contentment and happiness. The priest class adopted a more practical approach, as all their ancient technology operated to its fullest potential by way of Force aptitude which meant they could no longer fully control their own technology. This led scientists from the priest class to experiment on living beings in an attempt to discern the Force's essence. These experiments took the form of dissection of animals and grafting of tissue into prisoners' bodies. The crimes of these vivisectionists did not go unnoticed, and as such these Rakata in the Unknown Regions had a monstrous reputation for brutality. This reputation was the reason many indigenous populations fought fiercely against their Rakatan overmasters.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

Rakatan society was organized into a tribal structure with each tribe following its own goals. Some were obsessed with finding new ways to try and reconnect to the Force, while others disregarded their past and as a result became more primitive.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> Within some worlds in the Rakatan Archipelago, priests and warrior classes united to wield the wondrous inventions of their ancestors. Among these enlightened worlds, the day-to-day bloodshed was lessened though the urge to reclaim their lost glories was powerful. On other worlds, the schism between the two classes led to open conflict, with the warring factions using weapons they barely understood that left the landscape pitted and glowing with radioactivity. Among these were barbarous tribes that believed their worlds represented all of creation and made war against other native species.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

The Rakata spoke their own native tongue known as [[Rakata (language)|Rakata]].<ref name="KOTORCG" /><ref name="Unknown Regions" /> Despite this, they were intelligent enough to pick up new information, including other languages, quickly. This was especially true of members of the priest class, who were more likely to understand the speech of outsiders.<ref name="Unknown Regions" />

==Technology==
{{Quote|Surely you know the glory of the Builders and their Infinite Empire. The fury of their weapons surpassed even my own might.|The World Razer|translated=1|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:StarForge-DotJ0.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The Star Forge in operation]]

Ancient Rakata relied upon Force-powered technology to conquer many worlds.<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> The Rakata's rise to power was fueled by a range of advanced devices that married the Force to high technology. Amongst these wonders of their forebears were planetary disruptor fields, builder droids, and [[skipship]]s.<ref name="Unknown Regions" /> They were considered one of a dozen ancient races that had developed self-aware automata. In fact, the Infinite Empire did not see the Force and technology as being concepts at odds with one another. They were known to have built self-aware machines powered in part by Force energies.<ref name="TNEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> It was recorded that the Rakata had at some point used mechano-organic technology elements that were infused with the dark side.<ref name="Rn" /> Their prison facility on Belsavis made use of teleportation technology that allowed a quick means of transportation from one site to another. In addition, they developed a form of [[Force Stasis/Legends|stasis]] technology that left individuals immobile though conscious of events and preserved them for centuries, a technology they used as a means of imprisonment. Furthermore, they were able to generate massive power cores as seen on Belsavis that drew energy from hyperspace and, if overloaded, were capable of destroying an entire star system with the effects spreading to nearby systems.<ref name="TOR" /> The Rakata invented the [[Force-drive]], the earliest form of the interstellar [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]. The Force-drive, however, was a severely limited device due to the fact that it relied on the Force to function. It was only capable of perceiving and traveling to worlds with a significant Force signature (i.e., a high degree of native life). As such, though diverse and far flung, the number of worlds under the Rakata's thumb was limited.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

[[Star Map]]s were placed on conquered worlds as a lasting monument to the power and scope of the Infinite Empire. Like many Rakatan technologies, the Star Maps were self-sustaining and capable of regeneration. Terraforming machines were also frequently used to modify a conquered world's climate, geology, flora, and fauna to meet the Builder's needs. In so doing, the Rakata transformed entire worlds and greatly influenced the development of native species. Temples were built on several worlds, such as Honoghr, Dantooine, and Lehon. The purpose of some of these temples was to house the Star Maps. The purpose of the Honoghr temple was unknown. One of the Rakata's most interesting inventions was a "[[mind prison]]," a peculiar box that trapped the mind of its victim. The only way for a prisoner to escape (a flaw discovered by a Rakata imprisoned for an exceptionally long time) was to take over the body of the next being to foolishly open the box. Revan very nearly suffered this fate after playing with one such device, but after winning a game of riddles with the Rakatan captive, he was released. Unfortunately, he could not figure out how to save the prisoner from bondage without imprisoning a replacement.<ref name="KOTOR" />

A virtually endless stream of supplies was needed to expedite the expansion of the Rakatan empire. This led to the creation of their greatest achievement that was needed to build anything its creators desired.<ref name="JvS:TEGF" /> To this end, the Rakata created the Star Forge in [[30,000 BBY]]. The Star Forge was the centerpiece of the Rakatan empire and the most advanced of their technological innovations. It was a massive [[Space station/Legends|space station]] fueled by the Lehon system's star and built for the mass production of war hardware. It alone was capable of meeting the entire Empire's demand for [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and [[Battle droid/Legends|war droid]] construction, yet such efficiency came at a terrible price. The Star Forge was, in part, powered by the dark side of the Force and was, therefore, highly corruptive. Rakatan scientists and engineers allowed the Star Forge to have access to near-limitless supplies of energy because they believed that they could control it, but they were wrong. As a semi-living entity, the Star Forge gorged on dark-side energies, and with time, it began to feed itself by manipulating its own creators.<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:TarisAudience-KOTOR.png|thumb|right|350px|The Taris dueling ring audience, containing, quite inexplicably [[in-universe]], Rakata sprites]]

The Rakata were created for the video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. Before that, the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|second edition rulebook for Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]] mentioned "alien traders from far off in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]" who might have given hyperspace technology to Humans. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' revealed that the Rakata were the original creators of the hyperdrive and that the Corellians, Duros, and various other civilizations adopted and modified it for their own needs after the fall of the Infinite Empire.
In ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', the player can find a Rakatan Band which has a description that reads:<blockquote>"''This simple device improves the wearer's ability to perceive the reality of their surroundings. The origin behind the item's name is unknown, but rumor has it that these bands were constructed as a defense against an ancient species of alien deceivers, who made absurd claims of dominance concerning their role in the galaxy. It is said this species of lying primitives went so far as to take credit for almost every major event in galactic history since the discovery of the hyperdrive.''"</blockquote> The above statement implies that the Rakata made contact with the greater [[galactic community]] in between the events of ''Knights of the Old Republic'' ([[3956 BBY]]) and ''Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'' ([[3951 BBY]]).

''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' stated that the Rakata might have altered the orbits of the planets of the Corellian System in spite of the fact that The New Essential Chronology had already made it clear that that was the work of an earlier civilization called the "[[Celestial/Legends|Architects]]". 

''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' claimed that the Rakata and their culture were completely wiped out by the Galactic Republic. However, ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'' later established that some Rakata fled to the Rakatan Archipelago.
